source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Exact source records mapped to established public labels; mapping is recorded for every verse and verified against source KJV annotations. Daniel, Hosea, Joel, Jonah, Micah, and Nahum have chapter-boundary differences.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the material, unusual proportions, and provincial setting explicit.
verses.before: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
verses.after: King Nebuchadnezzar made a gold statue, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the full hierarchy rather than collapsing the ceremonial list.
verses.before: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.after: Then King Nebuchadnezzar summoned the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial officials to the dedication of the statue he had set up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent to gather the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces to come to the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

verses.rationale: Repeats the offices and statue language to retain the scene’s ceremonial weight.
verses.before: Then the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.after: So the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the provincial officials assembled for the dedication of King Nebuchadnezzar’s statue. They stood before the statue Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the satraps, prefects, governors, counselors, treasurers, judges, magistrates, and all the officials of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood before the image that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

verses.rationale: Keeps the threefold audience and direct proclamation.
verses.before: Then the herald proclaimed with strength, “To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages:
verses.after: A herald called out loudly, “Peoples, nations, and languages, this is the command for you:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the herald proclaimed with strength, “To you it is commanded, peoples, nations, and languages:

verses.rationale: Retains six instrument names with identification uncertainty reserved for a note.
verses.before: At the time you hear the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you will fall down and bow before the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
verses.after: When you hear the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the time you hear the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, you shall fall down and bow before the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.

verses.rationale: Preserves immediate lethal coercion and both required actions.
verses.before: Whoever does not fall down and bow will immediately be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire.”
verses.after: Anyone who does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Whoever does not fall down and bow shall immediately be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the shorter instrument list here rather than harmonizing it with verse5.
verses.before: So at that time, when all the peoples heard the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and bowed before the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.after: So when all the peoples heard the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and worshiped the gold statue King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore at that time, when all the peoples heard the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations, and languages fell down and bowed before the golden image that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

verses.rationale: Renders the malicious-accusation idiom naturally without inventing a charge.
verses.before: So at that time certain Chaldean men came near and maliciously accused the Judeans.
verses.after: At that time some Chaldeans came forward and accused the Jews.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore at that time certain Chaldean men came near and maliciously accused the Judeans.

verses.rationale: Preserves the formal wish introducing their accusation.
verses.before: They answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, live forever!
verses.after: They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “May the king live forever!
verses.tsw_comparator: They answered and said to King Nebuchadnezzar, “O king, live forever!

verses.rationale: Maintains the accusers’ full repetition of the decree.
verses.before: You, O king, made a decree that every person who hears the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music will fall down and bow before the golden image,
verses.after: You, O king, issued a command that everyone who hears the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music must fall down and worship the gold statue.
verses.tsw_comparator: You, O king, made a decree that every person who hears the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music shall fall down and bow before the golden image,

verses.rationale: Repeats the threatened punishment as part of their report.
verses.before: and whoever does not fall down and bow will be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire.
verses.after: Anyone who does not fall down and worship must be thrown into a blazing furnace.
verses.tsw_comparator: and whoever does not fall down and bow shall be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire.

verses.rationale: Follows the singular god in the reading note and names the appointees.
verses.before: There are certain Judean men whom you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men have paid no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not bow before the golden image that you set up.”
verses.after: But there are Jews you appointed to administer the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego—who pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your god or worship the gold statue you set up.”
verses.tsw_comparator: There are certain Judean men whom you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. These men have paid no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not bow before the golden image that you set up.”

verses.rationale: Makes the summons and its execution clear while preserving the repetition.
verses.before: Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men were brought before the king.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar flew into a rage and ordered Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego brought before him. The men were brought to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Nebuchadnezzar, in rage and fury, commanded that Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego be brought. Then these men were brought before the king.

verses.rationale: Retains the king’s plural gods, distinct from the preceding reading-note singular.
verses.before: Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not bow before the golden image that I have set up?
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar asked them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, that you do not serve my gods or worship the gold statue I set up?
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuchadnezzar answered and said to them, “Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods and do not bow before the golden image that I have set up?

verses.rationale: Preserves the offer, repeated list, threat, and challenge without softening royal violence.
verses.before: Now if you are ready, at the time you hear the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and bow before the image that I made. But if you do not bow, you will immediately be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire. And who is the god who will rescue you from my hand?”
verses.after: Now, if you are ready, when you hear the horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and worship the statue I made. But if you will not worship, you will immediately be thrown into a blazing furnace. What god could rescue you from my hand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if you are ready, at the time you hear the sound of horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe, and every kind of music, fall down and bow before the image that I made. But if you do not bow, you shall immediately be thrown into the midst of a furnace of blazing fire. And who is the god who will rescue you from my hand?”

verses.rationale: Keeps their direct address and refusal of a defense.
verses.before: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered and said to the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you concerning this matter.
verses.after: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego answered the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we do not need to defend ourselves to you in this matter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego answered and said to the king, “Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer you concerning this matter.

verses.rationale: Retains the conditional opening and distinction between ability and the following assurance.
verses.before: If it is so, our God whom we serve can rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire, and from your hand, O king, he will rescue us.
verses.after: If that is so, our God whom we serve is able to rescue us from the blazing furnace, and he will rescue us from your hand, O king.
verses.tsw_comparator: If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire, and from your hand, O king, he will rescue us.

verses.rationale: Leaves the conditional refusal terse and follows the singular divine designation in the reading note.
verses.before: But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and will not bow before the golden image that you have set up.”
verses.after: But even if not, know this, O king: we will not serve your god or worship the gold statue you set up.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods and will not bow before the golden image that you have set up.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the facial change and stated sevenfold heating.
verses.before: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the expression of his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He answered and commanded that the furnace be heated seven times more than it was normally heated.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and his expression changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego. He ordered the furnace heated seven times hotter than usual.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the expression of his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He answered and commanded that the furnace be heated seven times more than it was normally heated.

verses.rationale: Preserves the soldiers’ strength and the order to bind the three men.
verses.before: He commanded certain mighty men from his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
verses.after: He ordered some of the strongest men in his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego and throw them into the blazing furnace.
verses.tsw_comparator: He commanded certain mighty men from his army to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.

verses.rationale: Retains the clothing list, with uncertain garment identifications noted separately.
verses.before: Then these men were bound in their cloaks, tunics, hats, and other garments and were thrown into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.
verses.after: The men were bound in their robes, trousers, turbans, and other clothes, and thrown into the blazing furnace.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these men were bound in their cloaks, tunics, hats, and other garments and were thrown into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.

verses.rationale: Makes the causal sequence audible and preserves the soldiers’ deaths.
verses.before: Because the king’s command was so urgent and the furnace was exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who lifted up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.
verses.after: The king’s order was urgent and the furnace so fiercely heated that the flames killed the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego up to it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because the king’s command was so urgent and the furnace was exceedingly hot, the flame of the fire killed those men who lifted up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

verses.rationale: Keeps the reiterated three, names, and bonds before the reversal.
verses.before: But these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.
verses.after: The three men—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego—fell bound into the blazing furnace.
verses.tsw_comparator: But these three men, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, fell bound into the midst of the furnace of blazing fire.

verses.rationale: Shapes the abrupt reaction and exchange for natural narrative pace.
verses.before: Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose quickly. He answered and said to his counselors, “Did we not throw three men bound into the midst of the fire?” They answered and said to the king, “Certainly, O king.”
verses.after: Then King Nebuchadnezzar leaped up in alarm. “Didn’t we throw three bound men into the fire?” he asked his advisers. “Certainly, O king,” they answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and rose quickly. He answered and said to his counselors, “Did we not throw three men bound into the midst of the fire?” They answered and said to the king, “Certainly, O king.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the pagan king’s divine-plural description without identifying the fourth figure.
verses.before: He answered and said, “Look, I see four men unbound, walking among the fire, and there is no harm to them. And the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”
verses.after: “Look!” he said. “I see four men walking free in the fire, and they are unharmed. The fourth looks like a son of the gods.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He answered and said, “Look, I see four men unbound, walking in the midst of the fire, and there is no harm to them. And the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.”

verses.rationale: Retains both commands, the title, and all three repeated names.
verses.before: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the furnace of blazing fire and answered and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the blazing furnace and called, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego came out of the fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Nebuchadnezzar approached the opening of the furnace of blazing fire and answered and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out and come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out from the midst of the fire.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four separate observations supporting their unharmed state.
verses.before: The satraps, prefects, governors, and king’s counselors gathered and saw these men, that the fire had no power over their bodies. The hair of their heads was not singed, their cloaks were not changed, and the smell of fire had not come upon them.
verses.after: The satraps, prefects, governors, and the king’s advisers gathered around them. They saw that the fire had no power over the men’s bodies: no hair on their heads was singed, their robes were unchanged, and not even the smell of fire clung to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: The satraps, prefects, governors, and king’s counselors gathered and saw these men, that the fire had no power over their bodies. The hair of their heads was not singed, their cloaks were not changed, and the smell of fire had not come upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s interpretation, bodily risk, and exclusive worship.
verses.before: Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his messenger and rescued his servants who trusted in him. They changed the king’s word and gave up their bodies rather than serve or bow before any god except their own God.
verses.after: Nebuchadnezzar said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego! He sent his angel and rescued his servants, who trusted him. They defied the king’s command and surrendered their bodies rather than serve or worship any god but their own God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nebuchadnezzar answered and said, “Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, who sent his messenger and rescued his servants who trusted in him. They changed the king’s word and gave up their bodies rather than serve or bow before any god except their own God.

verses.rationale: Retains the new decree’s violence rather than turning the king’s praise into tolerance.
verses.before: So I make a decree that any people, nation, or language that speaks anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego will be torn limb from limb, and their houses will be made a refuse heap, because there is no other god who can rescue in this way.”
verses.after: I therefore decree that anyone of any people, nation, or language who speaks against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego will be torn limb from limb, and their house reduced to a refuse heap. No other god can rescue like this.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I make a decree that any people, nation, or language that speaks anything offensive against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego shall be torn limb from limb, and their houses shall be made a refuse heap, because there is no other god who is able to rescue in this way.”

verses.rationale: Renders their prospering under royal authority without inventing specific offices.
verses.before: Then the king caused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to prosper in the province of Babylon.
verses.after: Then the king advanced Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego in the province of Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king caused Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to prosper in the province of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the royal letter’s universal greeting and public numbering.
verses.before: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace increase.
verses.after: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations, and languages throughout the earth: May your well-being increase!
verses.tsw_comparator: King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: May your peace increase.

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s first-person testimony and double expression.
verses.before: It has seemed good to me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done toward me.
verses.after: I am pleased to tell you about the signs and wonders the Most High God has done for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: It has seemed good to me to declare the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done toward me.

verses.rationale: Maintains the praise as poetry and repeats kingdom.
verses.before: How great are his signs, and how mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his rule is from generation to generation.
verses.after: How great are his signs! How mighty his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his rule endures through every generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: How great are his signs, and how mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his rule is from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Preserves prosperity before the troubling vision.
verses.before: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
verses.after: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my home and flourishing in my palace.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.

verses.rationale: Separates the dream’s arrival from the continuing disturbance.
verses.before: I saw a dream, and it frightened me. The thoughts upon my bed and the visions of my head terrified me.
verses.after: Then I had a dream that frightened me. As I lay in bed, the images and visions in my mind alarmed me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw a dream, and it frightened me. The thoughts upon my bed and the visions of my head terrified me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the stated purpose of the royal summons.
verses.before: So a decree went out from me to bring before me all the wise men of Babylon so that they might reveal to me the interpretation of the dream.
verses.after: I ordered all Babylon’s wise men brought before me to tell me what the dream meant.
verses.tsw_comparator: So a decree went out from me to bring before me all the wise men of Babylon so that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.

verses.rationale: Preserves four specialist groups and the contrast between hearing and interpreting.
verses.before: Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners came in, and I told the dream before them, but they did not make its interpretation known to me.
verses.after: The magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners came in. I told them the dream, but they could not tell me its meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners came in, and I told the dream before them, but they did not make its interpretation known to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps Nebuchadnezzar’s religious vocabulary and explanation of the new name.
verses.before: At last Daniel came in before me, whose name is Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. I told the dream before him:
verses.after: At last Daniel came before me. He is called Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him the dream:
verses.tsw_comparator: At last Daniel came in before me, whose name is Belteshazzar according to the name of my god, and in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. I told the dream before him:

verses.rationale: Retains the request for both visions and interpretation despite the following retelling.
verses.before: “Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no mystery is too difficult for you, tell me the visions of my dream that I saw and its interpretation.
verses.after: “Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no mystery defeats you. Tell me the visions of the dream I saw and their meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you and no mystery is too difficult for you, tell me the visions of my dream that I saw and its interpretation.

verses.rationale: Makes the shift into dream description clear and retains the earth’s center.
verses.before: These were the visions of my head upon my bed: I was looking, and look, a tree was among the earth, and its height was great.
verses.after: These were the visions in my mind as I lay in bed: I saw a tree in the middle of the earth, enormously tall.
verses.tsw_comparator: These were the visions of my head upon my bed: I was looking, and behold, a tree was in the midst of the earth, and its height was great.

verses.rationale: Keeps the universal height-and-visibility imagery.
verses.before: The tree grew and became strong; its height reached to the heavens, and it was visible to the end of the entire earth.
verses.after: The tree grew large and strong. Its top reached the heavens, and it could be seen to the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The tree grew and became strong; its height reached to the heavens, and it was visible to the end of the whole earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves the successive beneficiaries and all-flesh conclusion.
verses.before: Its leaves were beautiful, and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field found shade under it, the birds of the heavens dwelt in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
verses.after: Its leaves were beautiful, its fruit abundant, and it held food for all. Wild animals found shade beneath it; the birds of the heavens lived in its branches. Every creature fed from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Its leaves were beautiful, and its fruit was abundant, and in it was food for all. The animals of the field found shade under it, the birds of the heavens dwelt in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.

verses.rationale: Keeps both designations for the descending figure.
verses.before: “I was looking in the visions of my head upon my bed, and look, a watcher, a holy one, came down from the heavens.
verses.after: As I watched the visions in my mind while lying in bed, a watcher, a holy one, came down from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I was looking in the visions of my head upon my bed, and look, a watcher, a holy one, came down from the heavens.

verses.rationale: Preserves every destructive command and displaced creature.
verses.before: He called with strength and said thus: ‘Cut down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.
verses.after: He called out loudly: ‘Cut down the tree and lop off its branches! Strip its leaves and scatter its fruit! Let the animals flee from beneath it and the birds from its branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: He called with strength and said thus: ‘Cut down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.

verses.rationale: Keeps the movement from tree to person without identifying it prematurely.
verses.before: But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, among the grass of the field. Let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.
verses.after: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze among the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven and share the grass of the earth with the animals.
verses.tsw_comparator: But leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, among the grass of the field. Let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the earth.

verses.rationale: Renders heart as mind here while retaining the unspecified unit times.
verses.before: Let his human heart be changed, and let the heart of an animal be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.
verses.after: Let his human mind be changed and an animal’s mind given to him. Let seven times pass over him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let his human heart be changed, and let the heart of an animal be given to him, and let seven times pass over him.

verses.rationale: Preserves heavenly decision and purpose without introducing a named historical ruler.
verses.before: The sentence is by decree of the watchers, and the matter by command of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills and sets over it the lowliest of people.’
verses.after: This sentence comes by the watchers’ decree, this decision by the holy ones’ command, so the living may know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms. He gives kingship to whomever he wishes and sets even the lowliest of people over it.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The sentence is by decree of the watchers, and the matter by command of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills and sets over it the lowliest of people.’

verses.rationale: Retains the king’s repeated explanation of Daniel’s ability.
verses.before: “This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. And you, Belteshazzar, tell the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make the interpretation known to me, but you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
verses.after: “This is the dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me what it means. None of my kingdom’s wise men can explain it to me, but you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “This dream I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. And you, Belteshazzar, tell the interpretation, because all the wise men of my kingdom are not able to make the interpretation known to me, but you are able, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves hesitation, reassurance, and the interpreter’s wish rather than a diagnosis.
verses.before: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts terrified him. The king answered and said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation terrify you.” Belteshazzar answered and said, “My lord, may the dream be for people who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
verses.after: Then Daniel, called Belteshazzar, was stunned for a while, his thoughts alarming him. The king said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its meaning alarm you.” Belteshazzar answered, “My lord, may the dream concern those who hate you, and its meaning your enemies!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was appalled for a moment, and his thoughts terrified him. The king answered and said, “Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation terrify you.” Belteshazzar answered and said, “My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!

verses.rationale: Repeats the dream’s identifying details before the interpretation.
verses.before: “The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, whose height reached to the heavens and was visible to all the earth,
verses.after: The tree you saw, which grew large and strong, whose top reached the heavens and which could be seen throughout the earth—
verses.tsw_comparator: “The tree that you saw, which grew and became strong, whose height reached to the heavens and was visible to all the earth,

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated abundance and shelter as a continuing sentence.
verses.before: whose leaves were beautiful and fruit abundant, in which was food for all, under which the animals of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the heavens lived—
verses.after: with its beautiful leaves, abundant fruit, and food for all, sheltering wild animals beneath it and birds of the heavens in its branches—
verses.tsw_comparator: whose leaves were beautiful and fruit abundant, in which was food for all, under which the animals of the field dwelt, and in whose branches the birds of the heavens lived—

verses.rationale: Makes the explicit identification emphatic and preserves the universal claim.
verses.before: it is you, O king. You have grown and become strong. Your greatness has grown and reaches to the heavens, and your rule to the end of the earth.
verses.after: that tree is you, O king. You have grown great and strong. Your greatness has reached the heavens, and your rule the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: it is you, O king. You have grown and become strong. Your greatness has grown and reaches to the heavens, and your rule to the end of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps the long retelling and its tree-to-person shift intact.
verses.before: And because the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, among the grass of the field; let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let his portion be with the animals of the field until seven times pass over him’—
verses.after: You saw a watcher, a holy one, descend from heaven and say, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave its stump and roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze among the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with heaven’s dew and share life with the wild animals until seven times pass over him.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And because the king saw a watcher, a holy one, coming down from the heavens and saying, ‘Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump of its roots in the earth, with a band of iron and bronze, among the grass of the field; let him be wet with the dew of the heavens, and let his portion be with the animals of the field until seven times pass over him’—

verses.rationale: Separates interpretation from the decree it interprets.
verses.before: this is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:
verses.after: This is its meaning, O king. This is the Most High’s decree that has come upon my lord the king:
verses.tsw_comparator: this is the interpretation, O king, and this is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:

verses.rationale: Preserves the loss of human dwelling and the knowledge that ends it.
verses.before: You will be driven away from humanity, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and you will be wet with the dew of the heavens. Seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills.
verses.after: You will be driven from human society and live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like cattle and be drenched with heaven’s dew. Seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives kingship to whomever he wishes.
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be driven away from humanity, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and you will be wet with the dew of the heavens. Seven times will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills.

verses.rationale: Retains Heaven as the ruling designation and the kingdom’s preservation.
verses.before: And as it was commanded to leave the stump of the tree’s roots, your kingdom will be established for you after you know that the heavens rule.
verses.after: The command to leave the tree’s stump and roots means your kingdom will remain for you once you know that Heaven rules.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as it was commanded to leave the stump of the tree’s roots, your kingdom will be established for you after you know that the heavens rule.

verses.rationale: Preserves right action and mercy, with the uncertain break/redeem sense noted separately.
verses.before: “Therefore, O king, let my counsel be pleasing to you: break with your sins by righteousness and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, so that perhaps there may be a lengthening of your prosperity.”
verses.after: So, O king, please accept my counsel: break with your sins by doing what is right, and with your wrongs by showing mercy to the poor. Perhaps your well-being may last longer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Therefore, O king, let my counsel be pleasing to you: break with your sins by righteousness and your iniquities by showing mercy to the poor, so that perhaps there may be a lengthening of your prosperity.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the concise narrative transition out of the royal account.
verses.before: All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.after: All this happened to King Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.tsw_comparator: All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.

verses.rationale: Retains the twelve-month interval and palace setting.
verses.before: At the end of twelve months he was walking upon the royal palace of Babylon.
verses.after: Twelve months later, he was walking on the roof of the royal palace in Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of twelve months he was walking upon the royal palace of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves the self-attribution and two purposes of royal boasting.
verses.before: The king answered and said, “Is this not great Babylon, which I myself have built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”
verses.after: The king said, “Isn’t this great Babylon, which I built as a royal residence by my mighty power and for my majestic glory?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered and said, “Is this not great Babylon, which I myself have built as a royal house by the strength of my power and for the glory of my majesty?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the immediate interruption and direct heavenly pronouncement.
verses.before: While the word was still in the king’s mouth, a voice fell from the heavens: “To you it is spoken, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has departed from you.
verses.after: While the words were still in the king’s mouth, a voice came from heaven: “King Nebuchadnezzar, this is said to you: Your kingship has been taken away.
verses.tsw_comparator: While the word was still in the king’s mouth, a voice fell from the heavens: “To you it is spoken, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has departed from you.

verses.rationale: Repeats the sentence without importing a fixed duration for times.
verses.before: You will be driven away from humanity, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and seven times will pass over you until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills.”
verses.after: You will be driven from human society and live with the wild animals. You will be made to eat grass like cattle. Seven times will pass over you until you know that the Most High rules over human kingdoms and gives kingship to whomever he wishes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You will be driven away from humanity, and your dwelling will be with the animals of the field. You will be made to eat grass like cattle, and seven times will pass over you until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wills.”

verses.rationale: Retains bodily degradation and the two animal comparisons.
verses.before: Immediately the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from humanity and ate grass like cattle. His body was wet with the dew of the heavens until his hair grew like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws.
verses.after: The sentence against Nebuchadnezzar took effect at once. He was driven from human society, ate grass like cattle, and was drenched with heaven’s dew. His hair grew like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws.
verses.tsw_comparator: Immediately the word was fulfilled upon Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from humanity and ate grass like cattle. His body was wet with the dew of the heavens until his hair grew like eagles’ feathers and his nails like birds’ claws.

verses.rationale: Marks the return to first person and distinguishes the concluding praise through lineation.
verses.before: “At the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my reason returned to me. I blessed the Most High and praised and honored the one who lives forever: For his rule is an everlasting rule, and his kingdom from generation to generation.
verses.after: At the end of those days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven, and my reason returned. I blessed the Most High and praised and honored the one who lives forever: His rule is everlasting, and his kingdom endures through every generation.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to the heavens, and my reason returned to me. I blessed the Most High and praised and honored the one who lives forever: For his rule is an everlasting rule, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

verses.rationale: Preserves the heaven-and-earth scope and the bodily restraint image.
verses.before: All the inhabitants of the earth are regarded as nothing, and he does according to his will among the army of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth. There is no one who can strike his hand or say to him, ‘What have you done?’
verses.after: All earth’s inhabitants count as nothing. He does as he wishes with heaven’s army and those who inhabit the earth. No one can hold back his hand or ask him, “What have you done?”
verses.tsw_comparator: All the inhabitants of the earth are regarded as nothing, and he does according to his will among the army of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth. There is no one who can strike his hand or say to him, ‘What have you done?’

verses.rationale: Keeps reason’s repetition and the sequence of royal restoration.
verses.before: At that time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and nobles sought me, and I was established over my kingdom, and extraordinary greatness was added to me.
verses.after: At that time my reason returned. My splendor and majesty returned with the glory of my kingdom. My advisers and nobles sought me out, I was restored to my kingdom, and still greater honor was given to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and splendor returned to me. My counselors and nobles sought me, and I was established over my kingdom, and extraordinary greatness was added to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves three praise verbs and the concluding reversal of pride.
verses.before: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of the heavens, for all his works are truth and his ways are justice, and people who walk in pride he can humble.”
verses.after: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of heaven. Everything he does is true, and all his ways are just. He is able to humble those who walk in pride.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt, and honor the King of the heavens, for all his works are truth and his ways are justice, and those who walk in pride he is able to humble.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the thousand guests and the king’s public drinking.
verses.before: King Belshazzar made a great feast for one thousand of his nobles, and before the thousand he drank wine.
verses.after: King Belshazzar held a great feast for a thousand of his nobles and drank wine in front of them.
verses.tsw_comparator: King Belshazzar made a great feast for one thousand of his nobles, and before the thousand he drank wine.

verses.rationale: Keeps the father designation and all participating groups without historical harmonization.
verses.before: While tasting the wine, Belshazzar commanded that the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought, so that the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them.
verses.after: As he tasted the wine, Belshazzar ordered the gold and silver vessels that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem’s temple brought in. The king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines were to drink from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: While tasting the wine, Belshazzar commanded that the gold and silver vessels that Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken from the temple in Jerusalem be brought, so that the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines might drink from them.

verses.rationale: Repeats the temple provenance and participants while retaining gold alone here.
verses.before: Then they brought the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
verses.after: So they brought the gold vessels taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem. The king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they brought the gold vessels that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king, his nobles, his wives, and his concubines drank from them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the six materials and connection between drinking and praise.
verses.before: They drank wine and praised gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
verses.after: They drank wine and praised gods of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.
verses.tsw_comparator: They drank wine and praised gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

verses.rationale: Keeps the visible fingers, material surface, and precise location.
verses.before: At that moment fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace, and the king saw the palm of the hand that was writing.
verses.after: At that moment, fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster wall of the royal palace, opposite the lampstand. The king watched the hand as it wrote.
verses.tsw_comparator: At that moment fingers of a human hand came out and wrote opposite the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the king’s palace, and the king saw the palm of the hand that was writing.

verses.rationale: Retains the bodily description rather than reducing it to fear alone.
verses.before: Then the king’s color changed, and his thoughts terrified him. The joints of his hips loosened, and his knees knocked against one another.
verses.after: The king turned pale. His thoughts terrified him; his hips gave way, and his knees knocked together.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king’s color changed, and his thoughts terrified him. The joints of his hips loosened, and his knees knocked against one another.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three rewards and the uncertain ordinal title without explanatory genealogy.
verses.before: The king called loudly to bring in the enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners. The king answered and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me will be clothed in purple, have a chain of gold around his neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”
verses.after: He shouted for the enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners. He told Babylon’s wise men, “Whoever reads this writing and explains it to me will wear purple, have a gold chain around his neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king called loudly to bring in the enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners. The king answered and said to the wise men of Babylon, “Whoever reads this writing and declares its interpretation to me shall be clothed in purple, have a chain of gold around his neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”

verses.rationale: Keeps inability to read distinct from inability to interpret.
verses.before: Then all the king’s wise men came in, but they were not able to read the writing or make its interpretation known to the king.
verses.after: All the king’s wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or explain it to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the king’s wise men came in, but they were not able to read the writing or make its interpretation known to the king.

verses.rationale: Preserves renewed fear and the separate reaction of his guests.
verses.before: Then King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, his color changed, and his nobles were perplexed.
verses.after: King Belshazzar grew even more terrified and turned pale. His nobles were bewildered.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, his color changed, and his nobles were perplexed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the queen unidentified beyond her title and echoes the symptoms she addresses.
verses.before: The queen, because of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet house. The queen answered and said, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you or your color change.
verses.after: The queen heard what the king and his nobles were saying and entered the banquet hall. “May the king live forever!” she said. “Do not let your thoughts terrify you; do not turn pale.
verses.tsw_comparator: The queen, because of the words of the king and his nobles, came into the banquet house. The queen answered and said, “O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you or your color change.

verses.rationale: Retains the queen’s divine plural and emphatic repetition of father.
verses.before: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father, illumination, insight, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners—your father the king—
verses.after: There is a man in your kingdom who has the spirit of the holy gods in him. In your father’s days he was found to have insight, understanding, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods. Your father, King Nebuchadnezzar—your father the king—appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father, illumination, insight, and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar your father appointed him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans, and diviners—your father the king—

verses.rationale: Keeps the three abilities and the knot-untying metaphor in natural English.
verses.before: because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, insight, interpretation of dreams, explanation of riddles, and solving of difficulties were found in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will declare the interpretation.”
verses.after: This Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar, was found to have an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, and understanding for interpreting dreams, explaining riddles, and unraveling difficulties. Summon Daniel now, and he will explain the meaning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge, insight, interpretation of dreams, explanation of riddles, and solving of difficulties were found in Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will declare the interpretation.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s emphasis on Daniel’s captive origin.
verses.before: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah whom the king my father brought from Judah?
verses.after: Daniel was brought before the king, who asked him, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah whom my father the king brought from Judah?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Are you Daniel, one of the exiles of Judah whom the king my father brought from Judah?

verses.rationale: Keeps gods without adding holy, absent from the king’s wording here.
verses.before: I have heard concerning you that the spirit of the gods is in you and that illumination, insight, and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.
verses.after: I have heard that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that you have insight, understanding, and exceptional wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: I have heard concerning you that the spirit of the gods is in you and that illumination, insight, and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.

verses.rationale: Retains the failed request before Daniel receives the offer.
verses.before: Now the wise men, the enchanters, were brought in before me to read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, but they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.
verses.after: The wise men and enchanters were brought before me to read this writing and explain it, but they could not tell me what it means.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the wise men, the enchanters, were brought in before me to read this writing and make its interpretation known to me, but they were not able to declare the interpretation of the matter.

verses.rationale: Repeats the promised honors and the conditional offer intact.
verses.before: Yet I have heard concerning you that you can give interpretations and solve difficulties. Now if you can read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you will be clothed in purple, have a chain of gold around your neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”
verses.after: I have heard that you can explain meanings and unravel difficulties. If you can read the writing and explain it to me, you will wear purple, have a gold chain around your neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have heard concerning you that you are able to give interpretations and solve difficulties. Now if you are able to read the writing and make its interpretation known to me, you shall be clothed in purple, have a chain of gold around your neck, and rule as third in the kingdom.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the refusal of payment distinct from willingness to interpret.
verses.before: Then Daniel answered and said before the king, “Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Even so, I will read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.
verses.after: Daniel answered the king, “Keep your gifts, and give your rewards to someone else. Still, I will read the writing for the king and explain its meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel answered and said before the king, “Let your gifts be for yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king and make the interpretation known to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four royal gifts and their giver.
verses.before: “O king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.
verses.after: O king, the Most High God gave your father Nebuchadnezzar kingship, greatness, glory, and majesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: “O king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father kingdom, greatness, glory, and majesty.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four parallel expressions of arbitrary royal power.
verses.before: Because of the greatness that he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. Whomever he wished he killed, and whomever he wished he kept alive; whomever he wished he raised up, and whomever he wished he humbled.
verses.after: Because of the greatness he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled in fear before him. He killed whomever he wished and kept alive whomever he wished; he raised up whomever he wished and brought low whomever he wished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of the greatness that he gave him, all peoples, nations, and languages trembled and feared before him. Whomever he wished he killed, and whomever he wished he kept alive; whomever he wished he raised up, and whomever he wished he humbled.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inward change and the two outward losses.
verses.before: But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit became strong in arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne, and his glory was removed from him.
verses.after: But when his heart grew proud and his spirit hardened into arrogance, he was deposed from his royal throne and stripped of his glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit became strong in arrogance, he was brought down from his royal throne, and his glory was removed from him.

verses.rationale: Retains wild donkeys, cattle, dew, and the conclusion learned through humiliation.
verses.before: He was driven from the children of humanity, his heart was made like that of an animal, and his dwelling was with wild donkeys. He was fed grass like cattle, and his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity and appoints over it whomever he wills.
verses.after: He was driven from human society, and his mind became like an animal’s. He lived among wild donkeys, was fed grass like cattle, and was drenched with heaven’s dew, until he knew that the Most High God rules over human kingdoms and appoints whomever he wishes to rule them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He was driven from the children of humanity, his heart was made like that of an animal, and his dwelling was with wild donkeys. He was fed grass like cattle, and his body was wet with the dew of the heavens, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of humanity and appoints over it whomever he wills.

verses.rationale: Preserves the charge of knowledgeable refusal and the stated son relationship.
verses.before: “But you, Belshazzar his son, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this.
verses.after: Yet you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, although you knew all this.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you, Belshazzar his son, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this.

verses.rationale: Keeps every group and material, including reordered silver/gold, and foregrounds the final contrast.
verses.before: Instead, you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of the heavens. The vessels of his house were brought before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see or hear or know. But the God in whose hand is your breath and to whom belong all your ways you have not honored.
verses.after: Instead, you raised yourself against the Lord of heaven. His temple’s vessels were brought before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which cannot see, hear, or know. But the God who holds your breath in his hand and owns all your ways—you did not honor him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead, you have lifted yourself up against the Lord of the heavens. The vessels of his house were brought before you, and you, your nobles, your wives, and your concubines drank wine from them. You praised gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone, which do not see or hear or know. But the God in whose hand is your breath and to whom belong all your ways you have not honored.

verses.rationale: Makes the explanatory link explicit without adding a human agent.
verses.before: So from his presence the palm of the hand was sent, and this writing was inscribed.
verses.after: That is why he sent the hand, and this writing was inscribed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore from his presence the palm of the hand was sent, and this writing was inscribed.

verses.rationale: Preserves the doubled first word and the inscription’s plural last form.
verses.before: “And this is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.
verses.after: “This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And this is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, PARSIN.

verses.rationale: Renders the counting wordplay and completion as Daniel’s explanation.
verses.before: This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
verses.after: Here is what the words mean: MENE—God has numbered the days of your kingship and brought it to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the interpretation of the matter: MENE—God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.

verses.rationale: Keeps the weighing image and adverse result.
verses.before: TEKEL—you have been weighed in the balances and found lacking.
verses.after: TEKEL—you have been weighed on the scales and found deficient.
verses.tsw_comparator: TEKEL—you have been weighed in the balances and found lacking.

verses.rationale: Retains the singular interpretive form and the named recipients of rule.

verses.tsw_comparator: PERES—your kingdom has been divided and given to the Medes and Persians.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the honors despite the earlier refusal, without inventing Daniel’s response.

verses.after: That very night Belshazzar, king of the Chaldeans, was killed.

verses.rationale: Preserves received, approximate age, and identity without identifying him with another ruler.

verses.after: Darius the Mede received the kingdom when he was about sixty-two years old.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old.

verses.rationale: Retains the reason for Daniel’s distinction and the appointment as an intention.
verses.before: Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the high officials and satraps because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over the whole kingdom.
verses.after: Daniel distinguished himself above the other administrators and satraps because he had an extraordinary spirit. The king planned to put him over the entire kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the high officials and satraps because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king planned to appoint him over the whole kingdom.

verses.rationale: Keeps the search within official duties and the repeated finding of integrity.

verses.after: The administrators and satraps looked for grounds to accuse Daniel in his conduct of the kingdom’s affairs. But they could find no negligence or corruption: he was trustworthy, and no fault or corruption was found in him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the high officials and satraps sought to find a ground for accusation against Daniel concerning the kingdom, but they were not able to find any ground for accusation or corruption, because he was faithful, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.

verses.rationale: Preserves their stated strategy without equating law with mere personal preference.
verses.before: Then these men said, “We will not find any ground for accusation against this Daniel unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.”
verses.after: The men said, “We will find no grounds against this Daniel unless we find something connected with the law of his God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these men said, “We will not find any ground for accusation against this Daniel unless we find it against him concerning the law of his God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the concerted approach and conventional greeting.
verses.before: Then these high officials and satraps came together before the king and said thus to him, “King Darius, live forever!
verses.after: So these administrators and satraps came together before the king. “King Darius, may you live forever!” they said.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these high officials and satraps came together before the king and said thus to him, “King Darius, live forever!

verses.rationale: Keeps their claim of unanimity as speech, all official ranks, and the thirty-day restriction.
verses.before: All the high officials of the kingdom, prefects, satraps, counselors, and governors have taken counsel to establish a royal statute and enforce an injunction that whoever makes a petition to any god or person for thirty days except to you, O king, will be thrown into a den of lions.
verses.after: “All the kingdom’s administrators, prefects, satraps, advisers, and governors have agreed that the king should establish and enforce this decree: for thirty days, anyone who petitions any god or person except you, O king, must be thrown into the lions’ den.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the high officials of the kingdom, prefects, satraps, counselors, and governors have taken counsel to establish a royal statute and enforce an injunction that whoever makes a petition to any god or person for thirty days except to you, O king, shall be thrown into a den of lions.

verses.rationale: Preserves the requested written authorization and asserted legal immutability.
verses.before: Now, O king, establish the injunction and sign the document so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”
verses.after: Now, O king, establish the decree and sign the document so it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now, O king, establish the injunction and sign the document so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the brief royal action without explaining motives.
verses.before: So King Darius signed the document, the injunction.
verses.after: So King Darius signed the document and the decree.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore King Darius signed the document, the injunction.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes existing open windows and habitual prayer from a newly staged act.
