verses.after: When Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went home. His upstairs room had windows open toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he knelt, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he went into his house. His windows in his upper room were open toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he knelt on his knees, prayed, and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.

verses.rationale: Preserves both petition and supplication in the discovery.
verses.before: Then these men came together and found Daniel making petition and seeking mercy before his God.
verses.after: The men came together and found Daniel praying and asking mercy before his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these men came together and found Daniel making petition and seeking mercy before his God.

verses.rationale: Maintains the full legal repetition before the accusation is disclosed.
verses.before: Then they approached and spoke before the king concerning the royal injunction: “Did you not sign an injunction that anyone who makes a petition to any god or person within thirty days except to you, O king, will be thrown into a den of lions?” The king answered and said, “The matter is certain, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”
verses.after: They approached the king about his decree: “Didn’t you sign a decree that for thirty days anyone who petitions any god or person except you, O king, must be thrown into the lions’ den?” The king answered, “The matter is settled, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they approached and spoke before the king concerning the royal injunction: “Did you not sign an injunction that anyone who makes a petition to any god or person within thirty days except to you, O king, shall be thrown into a den of lions?” The king answered and said, “The matter is certain, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked.”

verses.rationale: Keeps their disparaging captive identification and repeated prayer count.
verses.before: Then they answered and said before the king, “Daniel, who is from the exiles of Judah, has paid no attention to you, O king, or to the injunction that you signed, but three times a day he makes his petition.”
verses.after: Then they told the king, “Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the decree you signed. He makes his petition three times a day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they answered and said before the king, “Daniel, who is from the exiles of Judah, has paid no attention to you, O king, or to the injunction that you signed, but three times a day he makes his petition.”

verses.rationale: Preserves distress and sustained rescue effort without claiming success.
verses.before: Then the king, when he heard the matter, was greatly distressed, and he set his heart on Daniel to rescue him. Until the sun went down he exerted himself to deliver him.
verses.after: When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed. He set his mind on rescuing Daniel and worked until sunset to save him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king, when he heard the matter, was greatly distressed, and he set his heart on Daniel to rescue him. Until the sun went down he exerted himself to deliver him.

verses.rationale: Repeats the officials’ legal pressure with its claim attributed to them.
verses.before: Then these men came together before the king and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no injunction or statute that the king establishes may be changed.”
verses.after: Then the men came together before the king and said, “Remember, O king: by the law of the Medes and Persians, no decree or statute the king establishes can be changed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then these men came together before the king and said to the king, “Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no injunction or statute that the king establishes may be changed.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the king’s order and renders his following words as a wish, noting the alternative assurance.
verses.before: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually—he will rescue you.”
verses.after: The king gave the order, and Daniel was brought in and thrown into the lions’ den. The king said to Daniel, “May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king commanded, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the den of lions. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Your God whom you serve continually—he will rescue you.”

verses.rationale: Retains both sets of seals and their purpose.
verses.before: A stone was brought and placed over the opening of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
verses.after: A stone was brought and laid over the den’s opening. The king sealed it with his own signet and those of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
verses.tsw_comparator: A stone was brought and placed over the opening of the den, and the king sealed it with his signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the obscure diversions term broad and preserves sleeplessness.
verses.before: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.
verses.after: The king returned to his palace and spent the night fasting. No diversions were brought to him, and sleep fled from him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.

verses.rationale: Retains urgency and the precise dawn setting.
verses.before: Then the king arose at dawn, at first light, and went hurriedly to the den of lions.
verses.after: At the first light of dawn, the king got up and hurried to the lions’ den.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king arose at dawn, at first light, and went hurriedly to the den of lions.

verses.rationale: Preserves the anxious question and echoes the earlier continual-service formula.
verses.before: When he came near the den to Daniel, he cried out with a grieving voice. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God whom you serve continually been able to rescue you from the lions?”
verses.after: As he approached the den, he called to Daniel in an anguished voice: “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When he came near the den to Daniel, he cried out with a grieving voice. The king answered and said to Daniel, “Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God whom you serve continually been able to rescue you from the lions?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the formal salutation before the rescue report.
verses.before: Then Daniel spoke with the king: “O king, live forever!
verses.after: Daniel answered the king, “May the king live forever!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel spoke with the king: “O king, live forever!

verses.rationale: Retains both divine innocence and the claim of no harm to the king.
verses.before: My God sent his messenger and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before him innocence was found in me, and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”
verses.after: My God sent his angel and shut the lions’ mouths. They have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. Nor have I done you any harm, O king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: My God sent his messenger and shut the mouths of the lions, and they did not harm me, because before him innocence was found in me, and also before you, O king, I have done no harm.”

verses.rationale: Repeats the lifting and keeps the narrator’s stated reason for safety.
verses.before: Then the king was exceedingly glad concerning him and commanded that Daniel be brought up from the den. So Daniel was brought up from the den, and no wound was found upon him because he had trusted in his God.
verses.after: The king was overjoyed and ordered Daniel lifted from the den. Daniel was lifted out, and no injury was found on him, because he had trusted his God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king was exceedingly glad concerning him and commanded that Daniel be brought up from the den. So Daniel was brought up from the den, and no wound was found upon him because he had trusted in his God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the killing of the families and the graphic violence without endorsement or euphemism.
verses.before: Then the king commanded, and they brought those men who had maliciously accused Daniel, and they threw them, their children, and their wives into the den of lions. They had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
verses.after: At the king’s command, the men who had accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions’ den, together with their children and wives. Before they reached the bottom, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king commanded, and they brought those men who had maliciously accused Daniel, and they threw them, their children, and their wives into the den of lions. They had not reached the bottom of the den before the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

verses.rationale: Keeps the royal proclamation’s threefold audience and recurring greeting.
verses.before: Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: “May your peace increase.
verses.after: Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages throughout the earth: “May your well-being increase!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Darius wrote to all peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: “May your peace increase.

verses.rationale: Separates the command from poetic praise while preserving compelled reverence.
verses.before: I make a decree that in every dominion of my kingdom people will tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: For he is the living God and endures forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his rule will be to the end.
verses.after: I decree that throughout my realm people must tremble in fear before Daniel’s God. For he is the living God, enduring forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed; his rule will last to the end.
verses.tsw_comparator: I make a decree that in every dominion of my kingdom people shall tremble and fear before the God of Daniel: For he is the living God and endures forever. His kingdom will not be destroyed, and his rule will be to the end.

verses.rationale: Retains parallel rescue verbs and the particular event concluding the praise.
verses.before: He rescues and delivers; he does signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth, for he has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”
verses.after: He rescues and delivers; he performs signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He rescued Daniel from the lions’ power.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He rescues and delivers; he does signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth, for he has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the two named reigns without resolving their historical relationship.
verses.before: So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.after: So Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and during the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
verses.tsw_comparator: So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

verses.rationale: Keeps the earlier reign setting and written first-person account that follows.
verses.before: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed. Then he wrote down the dream. He told the summary of the matter.
verses.after: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream and visions in his mind as he lay in bed. He wrote down the dream, giving an account of what he saw.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel saw a dream and visions of his head upon his bed. Then he wrote down the dream. He told the summary of the matter.

verses.rationale: Preserves the visionary frame and four winds acting on the sea.
verses.before: Daniel answered and said: “I was looking in my vision by night, and look, the four winds of the heavens were stirring up the great sea.
verses.after: Daniel said: In my night vision I saw the four winds of heaven churning the great sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel answered and said: “I was looking in my vision by night, and look, the four winds of the heavens were stirring up the great sea.

verses.rationale: Keeps number, origin, and difference before individual descriptions.

verses.after: Four great beasts came up from the sea, each different from the others.
verses.tsw_comparator: Four great beasts came up from the sea, each different from the others.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three-stage humanizing transformation without identifying an emperor.
verses.before: The first was like a lion and had wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off, and it was lifted from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a human being, and a human heart was given to it.
verses.after: The first was like a lion with eagle’s wings. As I watched, its wings were plucked off. It was lifted from the ground, made to stand on two feet like a human being, and given a human mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first was like a lion and had wings of an eagle. I watched until its wings were torn off, and it was lifted from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a human being, and a human heart was given to it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the asymmetry, three ribs, and violent command.
verses.before: And look, another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. And thus they said to it: ‘Rise, devour much flesh!’
verses.after: Then I saw a second beast, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, with three ribs between its teeth. It was told, “Get up! Devour plenty of flesh!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And look, another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. And thus they said to it: ‘Rise, devour much flesh!’

verses.rationale: Preserves both fours and the passive grant of authority.
verses.before: After this I was looking, and look, another, like a leopard. It had four wings of a bird on its back, and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.
verses.after: After that I saw another, like a leopard, with four bird’s wings on its back. The beast had four heads, and authority to rule was given to it.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this I was looking, and look, another, like a leopard. It had four wings of a bird on its back, and the beast had four heads, and dominion was given to it.

verses.rationale: Maintains the unnamed beast’s triple terror and distinct destructive actions.

verses.after: After that, in my night visions, I saw a fourth beast—terrifying, dreadful, and immensely strong. It had huge iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, trampling what remained underfoot. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.
verses.tsw_comparator: After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and look, a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and exceedingly strong. It had great iron teeth. verses.rationale: Keeps the small horn’s displacement of three and its humanlike features.

verses.rationale: Retains the plural thrones, ancient title, whiteness comparisons, and fiery wheels.
verses.before: “I watched until thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days sat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was flames of fire; its wheels were burning fire.
verses.after: I watched until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white as snow, the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was flames of fire; its wheels were burning fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves the numerical expressions and judicial setting as poetry.
verses.before: A river of fire flowed and came out from before him. A thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat, and the books were opened.
verses.after: A river of fire flowed out before him. A thousand thousands served him; ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court took its seat, and the books were opened.
verses.tsw_comparator: A river of fire flowed and came out from before him. A thousand thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat, and the books were opened.

verses.rationale: Keeps the horn’s speech connected to the beast’s judgment.
verses.before: “I watched then because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed, and its body was destroyed and given over to be burned with fire.
verses.after: I kept watching because of the arrogant words the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed, its body destroyed and given over to the burning fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I watched then because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking. I watched until the beast was killed, and its body was destroyed and given over to be burned with fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distinction between loss of rule and continued life.
verses.before: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but an extension of life was given to them for a time and a season.
verses.after: The other beasts had their authority taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was taken away, but an extension of life was given to them for a time and a season.

verses.rationale: Keeps the humanlike description, clouds, and movement toward the enthroned figure.
verses.before: “I was looking in the visions of the night, and look, with the clouds of the heavens one like a son of man was coming. He came to the Ancient of Days and was brought near before him.
verses.after: In my night visions I saw someone like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven. He approached the Ancient of Days and was presented before him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “I was looking in the visions of the night, and look, with the clouds of the heavens one like a son of man was coming. He came to the Ancient of Days and was brought near before him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold grant, universal service, and two assurances of permanence.

verses.after: He was given authority, glory, and kingship, so that all peoples, nations, and languages would serve him. His rule is an everlasting rule that will not pass away, and his kingdom will never be destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: To him were given dominion, glory, and kingdom, so that all peoples, nations, and languages should serve him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion that will not pass away, and his kingdom one that will not be destroyed.

verses.rationale: Renders the bodily sheath idiom naturally while retaining Daniel’s distress.

verses.after: My spirit was distressed within me, Daniel, and the visions in my mind alarmed me.
verses.tsw_comparator: “As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within me, and the visions of my head terrified me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the interpreter initially unnamed and distinguishes request from answer.

verses.after: I approached one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. He told me and explained what it meant:

verses.rationale: Retains kings and earth rather than harmonizing the earlier sea image.

verses.after: “These four great beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps bronze claws as an additional detail in Daniel’s renewed question.

verses.after: Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others and so terrifying. It had iron teeth and bronze claws; it devoured and crushed, trampling what remained underfoot.

verses.tsw_comparator: I was watching, and that horn made war with the holy ones and prevailed over them,

verses.rationale: Keeps judgment’s favorable sense with the alternative grant of judging authority noted.
verses.before: until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came when the holy ones possessed the kingdom.
verses.after: until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High. The time arrived, and the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given for the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came when the holy ones possessed the kingdom.

verses.rationale: Preserves the explanation’s shift from kings to kingdom and its three destructive verbs.
verses.before: “Thus he said: ‘The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, different from all the kingdoms. It will devour the entire earth, trample it down, and crush it.
verses.after: He said, “The fourth beast is a fourth kingdom on earth, different from every other kingdom. It will devour the whole earth, trample it, and crush it.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus he said: ‘The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, different from all the kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trample it down, and crush it.

verses.rationale: Keeps every number and the later king’s difference without supplying identities.
verses.before: As for the ten horns, from this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He will be different from the former ones and will humble three kings.
verses.after: The ten horns are ten kings who will arise from that kingdom. Another will arise after them, different from the earlier ones, and bring down three kings.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the ten horns, from this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He will be different from the former ones and will humble three kings.

verses.rationale: Preserves the attack on time and law, the ambiguous they, and the symbolic duration.
verses.before: He will speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will intend to change times and law, and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time.
verses.after: He will speak against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will intend to change appointed times and law. They will be handed over to him for a time, times, and half a time.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will intend to change times and law, and they will be given into his hand for a time, times, and half a time.

verses.rationale: Retains judicial removal and the double expression of final destruction.
verses.before: But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to destroy and bring it to an end until the end.
verses.after: But the court will sit, and his authority will be taken away, destroyed and abolished completely.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the court will sit, and his dominion will be taken away, to destroy and bring it to an end until the end.

verses.rationale: Keeps the people-of-holy-ones construction and singular final pronouns open for a note.
verses.before: Then the kingdom, the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.’
verses.after: The kingship, authority, and greatness of the kingdoms under all heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all authorities will serve and obey him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the kingdom, the dominion, and the greatness of the kingdoms under all the heavens will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions will serve and obey him.’

verses.rationale: Preserves the closing bodily response and private retention of the vision.
verses.before: “Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly terrified me and my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart.”
verses.after: That is the end of the account. I, Daniel, was deeply alarmed by my thoughts, and I turned pale. But I kept the matter in my heart.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Here is the end of the matter. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly terrified me and my color changed, but I kept the matter in my heart.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the later date within Belshazzar’s reign and link to the preceding vision.
verses.before: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that appeared to me at first.
verses.after: In the third year of King Belshazzar’s reign, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one I had seen earlier.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that appeared to me at first.

verses.rationale: Makes the location visionary without claiming an ordinary journey.
verses.before: I saw in the vision, and when I saw, I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision, and I was beside the Ulai canal.
verses.after: In the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. As I watched the vision, I was beside the Ulai canal.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw in the vision, and when I saw, I was in Susa the citadel, which is in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision, and I was beside the Ulai canal.

verses.rationale: Retains the order and inequality of the two horns.
verses.before: I lifted my eyes and saw, and look, a ram standing before the canal with two horns. The two horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.
verses.after: I looked up and saw a ram standing beside the canal. It had two long horns, one longer than the other; the longer one had grown up later.
verses.tsw_comparator: I lifted my eyes and saw, and look, a ram standing before the canal with two horns. The two horns were high, but one was higher than the other, and the higher one came up last.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three directions and unchecked agency.
verses.before: I saw the ram charging westward, northward, and southward. No animal could stand before it, and there was no one who could rescue from its hand. It did according to its will and became great.
verses.after: I saw the ram charging west, north, and south. No animal could stand against it, and none could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and became great.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw the ram charging westward, northward, and southward. No animal could stand before it, and there was no one who could rescue from its hand. It did according to its will and became great.

verses.rationale: Keeps the extraordinary movement and single prominent horn.
verses.before: While I was considering, look, a male goat came from the west across the face of the entire earth without touching the ground, and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
verses.after: As I was considering this, a male goat came from the west, crossing the whole earth without touching the ground. It had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
verses.tsw_comparator: While I was considering, look, a male goat came from the west across the face of the whole earth without touching the ground, and the goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated ram identification and violent rush.
verses.before: It came to the ram with the two horns that I had seen standing before the canal and ran at it in the fury of its strength.
verses.after: It came toward the two-horned ram I had seen beside the canal and charged at it in furious strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: It came to the ram with the two horns that I had seen standing before the canal and ran at it in the fury of its strength.

verses.rationale: Retains the full sequence of attack, helplessness, and trampling.
verses.before: I saw it come close to the ram, and it became enraged against it. It struck the ram and broke its two horns, and there was no strength in the ram to stand before it. It threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its hand.
verses.after: I saw it close in on the ram, raging against it. It struck the ram and broke both its horns. The ram had no strength to resist. The goat hurled it to the ground and trampled it, and no one could rescue the ram from its power.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw it come close to the ram, and it became enraged against it. It struck the ram and broke its two horns, and there was no strength in the ram to stand before it. It threw it to the ground and trampled it, and there was no one to rescue the ram from its hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the breaking at peak strength and fourfold replacement.
verses.before: Then the male goat became exceedingly great. But when it was strong, the great horn was broken, and in its place four conspicuous horns came up toward the four winds of the heavens.
verses.after: The male goat became exceedingly great. But at the height of its strength, its great horn was broken. Four conspicuous horns grew up in its place toward the four winds of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the male goat became exceedingly great. But when it was strong, the great horn was broken, and in its place four conspicuous horns came up toward the four winds of the heavens.

verses.rationale: Leaves them unspecified between the preceding horns and winds and retains the land’s epithet.
verses.before: From one of them came a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Beautiful Land.
verses.after: From one of them came a small horn. It grew immensely toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Beautiful Land.
verses.tsw_comparator: From one of them came a little horn, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east, and toward the Beautiful Land.

verses.rationale: Keeps celestial imagery without substituting its interpreted human referents.
verses.before: It grew as great as the host of the heavens and caused some of the host and some of the stars to fall to the earth, and it trampled them.
verses.after: It grew as high as heaven’s host, threw some of the host and stars to the earth, and trampled them.
verses.tsw_comparator: It grew as great as the host of the heavens and caused some of the host and some of the stars to fall to the earth, and it trampled them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the passive removal in the reading note and consequential pronoun reference.
verses.before: It even grew great up to the Prince of the host. From him the continual offering was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
verses.after: It exalted itself even against the Prince of the host. The regular offering was taken away from him, and the site of his sanctuary was thrown down.
verses.tsw_comparator: It even grew great up to the Prince of the host. From him the continual offering was taken away, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.

verses.rationale: Retains the obscure host/offering relation and identifies the feminine acting subject as the horn.
verses.before: A host was given over with the continual offering because of transgression, and it threw truth to the ground. It acted and prospered.
verses.after: Because of rebellion, a host was handed over along with the regular offering. The horn threw truth to the ground and prospered in what it did.
verses.tsw_comparator: A host was given over with the continual offering because of transgression, and it threw truth to the ground. It acted and prospered.

verses.rationale: Preserves all elements of the question without making the omitted offering action explicit twice.
verses.before: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, “Until when is the vision concerning the continual offering, the transgression that causes desolation, and the giving over of sanctuary and host to be trampled?”
verses.after: I heard a holy one speaking. Another holy one asked the one who was speaking, “How long will the vision last—the regular offering, the rebellion that devastates, and the giving over of sanctuary and host to be trampled?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, “Until when is the vision concerning the continual offering, the transgression that causes desolation, and the giving over of sanctuary and host to be trampled?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the time expression unconverted and the broad vindication/restoration sense.
verses.before: He said to me, “For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be restored to its rightful state.”
verses.after: He answered me, “For 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary will be set right.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, “For two thousand three hundred evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary shall be restored to its rightful state.”

verses.rationale: Retains Daniel’s search and the humanlike appearance rather than prematurely naming Gabriel.
verses.before: When I, Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought understanding. Then look, standing before me was one with the appearance of a man.
verses.after: When I, Daniel, had seen the vision and was trying to understand it, someone with the appearance of a man stood before me.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I, Daniel, had seen the vision, I sought understanding. Then look, standing before me was one with the appearance of a man.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the canal setting while preserving the voice’s human description.
verses.before: I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it called and said, “Gabriel, make this one understand the vision.”
verses.after: I heard a human voice from between the banks of the Ulai calling, “Gabriel, help this man understand the vision.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I heard a human voice between the banks of the Ulai, and it called and said, “Gabriel, make this one understand the vision.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the address and end-time statement without fixing a later chronology.
verses.before: So he came near where I stood. When he came, I was terrified and fell on my face. But he said to me, “Understand, son of man, that the vision is for the time of the end.”
verses.after: He came near where I stood. I was terrified at his approach and fell facedown. He said to me, “Understand, son of man: the vision concerns the time of the end.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So he came near where I stood. When he came, I was terrified and fell on my face. But he said to me, “Understand, son of man, that the vision is for the time of the end.”

verses.rationale: Retains sleep, touch, and restoration to standing.
verses.before: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. But he touched me and made me stand where I had stood.
verses.after: As he spoke to me, I fell into a deep sleep, facedown on the ground. He touched me and stood me on my feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. But he touched me and made me stand where I had stood.

verses.rationale: Keeps wrath and appointed end as the explanation’s temporal frame.
verses.before: He said, “Look, I am making known to you what will be at the latter time of wrath, for it concerns the appointed time of the end.
verses.after: He said, “I will tell you what will happen in the final period of wrath, for the end comes at its appointed time.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Look, I am making known to you what will be at the latter time of wrath, for it concerns the appointed time of the end.

verses.rationale: Names the two kingdoms only where the source names them.
verses.before: “The ram that you saw with the two horns: these are the kings of Media and Persia.
verses.after: The two-horned ram you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The ram that you saw with the two horns: these are the kings of Media and Persia.

verses.rationale: Retains shaggy and the first-king designation without adding a personal name.
verses.before: The hairy goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
verses.after: The shaggy goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
verses.tsw_comparator: The hairy goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.

verses.rationale: Keeps the nation’s unity and diminished strength of the successor kingdoms.
verses.before: As for the horn that was broken and four that arose in its place, four kingdoms will arise from his nation, but not with his strength.
verses.after: The broken horn and the four that arose in its place mean four kingdoms will arise from that nation, but without his strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the horn that was broken and four that arose in its place, four kingdoms will arise from his nation, but not with his strength.

verses.rationale: Preserves rebels and the enigmatic skill rather than translating it entirely as political cunning.
verses.before: “At the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors have completed their transgression, a king fierce of face and understanding riddles will arise.
verses.after: Toward the end of their reign, when the rebels have reached their full measure, a fierce-faced king, skilled in riddles, will arise.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors have completed their transgression, a king fierce of face and understanding riddles will arise.

verses.rationale: Retains the paradox of power and both groups destroyed.
verses.before: His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will destroy extraordinarily and prosper and act. He will destroy mighty ones and the people of the holy ones.
verses.after: His power will grow strong, though not by his own power. He will cause extraordinary destruction, succeed in what he does, and destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will destroy extraordinarily and prosper and act. He will destroy mighty ones and the people of the holy ones.

verses.rationale: Preserves deceptive success, attack on security, and nonhuman ending.
verses.before: By his cunning he will make deceit prosper in his hand. He will grow great in his heart, and in ease he will destroy many. He will rise against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken—not by human hand.
verses.after: Through his cunning he will make deceit succeed. In his heart he will exalt himself, and he will destroy many while they are at ease. He will stand against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken without a human hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: By his cunning he will make deceit prosper in his hand. He will grow great in his heart, and in ease he will destroy many. He will rise against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken—not by human hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the authentication and command to preserve the vision for a distant time.
verses.before: “The vision of the evenings and mornings that was spoken is true. But you, seal up the vision, for it concerns many days from now.”
verses.after: The vision of the evenings and mornings that was told is true. But you must seal up the vision, for it concerns days far ahead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “The vision of the evenings and mornings that was spoken is true. But you, seal up the vision, for it concerns many days from now.”

verses.rationale: Preserves illness, resumed service, and unresolved comprehension after the explanation.
verses.before: Then I, Daniel, was exhausted and sick for days. Afterward I rose and did the king’s business. But I was appalled by the vision, and there was no one who understood it.
verses.after: I, Daniel, was exhausted and ill for days. Then I got up and returned to the king’s work. I was appalled by the vision and could not understand it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I, Daniel, was exhausted and sick for days. Afterward I rose and did the king’s business. But I was appalled by the vision, and there was no one who understood it.

verses.rationale: Preserves the father, ancestry, and passive royal appointment in an opening continued across labels.
verses.before: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the offspring of the Medes, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans—
verses.after: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, a Mede who had been made king over the Chaldean kingdom—
verses.tsw_comparator: In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, from the offspring of the Medes, who was made king over the kingdom of the Chaldeans—

verses.rationale: Keeps the book-based reflection and exact seventy-year period.
verses.before: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years concerning which the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, for the completion of the desolations of Jerusalem: seventy years.
verses.after: in the first year of his reign—I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years the LORD had spoken of to Jeremiah the prophet: Jerusalem’s desolation was to last seventy years.
verses.tsw_comparator: in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years concerning which the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet, for the completion of the desolations of Jerusalem: seventy years.

verses.rationale: Retains the physical acts accompanying the appeal.
verses.before: I set my face toward the Lord God to seek him with prayer and pleas, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
verses.after: I turned toward the Lord God, seeking him in prayer and pleas for mercy, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.
verses.tsw_comparator: I set my face toward the Lord God to seek him with prayer and pleas, with fasting, sackcloth, and ashes.

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine designations and the covenant-love pairing.
verses.before: I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession and said: “Please, Lord, the great and fearsome God, keeping covenant and steadfast love with people who love him and keep his commandments,
verses.after: I prayed to the LORD my God and confessed: “Please, Lord, great and awe-inspiring God, who keeps covenant and faithful love with those who love him and keep his commandments:
verses.tsw_comparator: I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession and said: “Please, Lord, the great and fearsome God, keeping covenant and steadfast love with those who love him and keep his commandments,

verses.rationale: Keeps the accumulation of confession rather than compressing it to a single fault.
verses.before: we have sinned and done wrong and acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and judgments.
verses.after: we have sinned and done wrong, acted wickedly and rebelled. We have turned away from your commandments and judgments.
verses.tsw_comparator: we have sinned and done wrong and acted wickedly and rebelled, turning aside from your commandments and judgments.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four audiences of the rejected prophetic speech.
verses.before: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our officials, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.
verses.after: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our leaders, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our officials, our ancestors, and all the people of the land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the contrast, bodily shame image, and full dispersed community.
verses.before: “To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as it is this day—to the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, those near and those far away, in all the lands where you drove them because of the unfaithfulness with which they acted against you.
verses.after: Righteousness belongs to you, Lord, but shame covers our faces, as it does today: the people of Judah, Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and all Israel, near and far, in all the lands where you drove them because they were unfaithful to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us shame of face, as it is this day—to the men of Judah, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and all Israel, those near and those far away, in all the lands where you drove them because of the unfaithfulness with which they acted against you.

verses.rationale: Retains YHWH distinct from Lord and the repeated confession of shame.
verses.before: O LORD, to us belongs shame of face, to our kings, our officials, and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
verses.after: LORD, shame covers our faces—our kings, our leaders, and our ancestors—because we have sinned against you.
verses.tsw_comparator: O LORD, to us belongs shame of face, to our kings, our officials, and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine mercy alongside acknowledged rebellion without erasing either.
verses.before: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.
verses.after: Mercy and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God, though we have rebelled against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.

verses.rationale: Retains obedience, walking, and plural instructions.
verses.before: We have not listened to the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in his instructions that he set before us by the hand of his servants the prophets.
verses.after: We have not obeyed the LORD our God or walked in the instructions he set before us through his servants the prophets.
verses.tsw_comparator: We have not listened to the voice of the LORD our God, to walk in his instructions that he set before us by the hand of his servants the prophets.

verses.rationale: Keeps the image of poured judgment and the shift from you to him.
verses.before: All Israel has transgressed your instruction and turned aside, refusing to listen to your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the instruction of Moses, servant of God, have been poured upon us, because we sinned against him.
verses.after: All Israel has transgressed your instruction and turned away, refusing to obey you. So the curse and sworn oath written in the instruction of Moses, God’s servant, have been poured out upon us, because we sinned against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: All Israel has transgressed your instruction and turned aside, refusing to listen to your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the instruction of Moses, servant of God, have been poured upon us, because we sinned against him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the reading-note singular word and the prayer’s unparalleled-disaster claim.
verses.before: He established his words that he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us by bringing upon us great disaster, for under all the heavens nothing has been done like what was done to Jerusalem.
verses.after: He has fulfilled the word he spoke against us and the rulers who ruled us, bringing great disaster upon us. Nothing under all heaven has been done like what was done to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: He established his words that he spoke against us and against our judges who judged us by bringing upon us great disaster, for under all the heavens nothing has been done like what was done to Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the turn from third to second person within the prayer.
verses.before: As it is written in the instruction of Moses, all this disaster came upon us, yet we did not seek the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our guilt and giving attention to your truth.
verses.after: All this disaster came upon us just as it is written in Moses’ instruction. Yet we did not seek the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our wrongdoing and giving attention to your truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is written in the instruction of Moses, all this disaster came upon us, yet we did not seek the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our guilt and giving attention to your truth.

verses.rationale: Retains watchfulness, explicit divine agency, and twice-named LORD.
verses.before: So the LORD watched over the disaster and brought it upon us, for the LORD our God is righteous in all the works that he has done, but we have not listened to his voice.
verses.after: The LORD kept watch over the disaster and brought it upon us. For the LORD our God is righteous in everything he has done, but we have not obeyed him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the LORD watched over the disaster and brought it upon us, for the LORD our God is righteous in all the works that he has done, but we have not listened to his voice.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exodus appeal and renewed confession.
verses.before: “And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out from the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made for yourself a name as it is this day—we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
verses.after: “And now, Lord our God, you brought your people out of Egypt with a strong hand and made a name for yourself that remains to this day. We have sinned; we have acted wickedly.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out from the land of Egypt with a strong hand and made for yourself a name as it is this day—we have sinned; we have acted wickedly.

verses.rationale: Keeps city/mountain parallel and communal responsibility without relocating blame.
verses.before: O Lord, according to all your righteous acts, please let your anger and fury turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the guilt of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to everyone who are around us.
verses.after: Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, please turn your anger and fury away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and our ancestors’ wrongdoing, Jerusalem and your people have become a disgrace to everyone around us.
verses.tsw_comparator: O Lord, according to all your righteous acts, please let your anger and fury turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. For because of our sins and the guilt of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a reproach to all who are around us.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unusual third-person Lord phrase and shining-face image.
verses.before: And now, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his pleas, and for your own sake, O Lord, cause your face to shine upon your desolate sanctuary.
verses.after: Now, our God, hear your servant’s prayer and pleas for mercy. For the Lord’s sake, let your face shine upon your desolate sanctuary.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his pleas, and for your own sake, O Lord, cause your face to shine upon your desolate sanctuary.

verses.rationale: Keeps ear and eye appeals and grounds the petition explicitly in mercy.
verses.before: Incline your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by your name. For we are not causing our pleas to fall before you because of our righteous acts, but because of your great compassion.
verses.after: My God, incline your ear and hear! Open your eyes and see our devastation and the city that bears your name. We lay our pleas before you because of your great mercy, not because of our righteous acts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Incline your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by your name. For we are not causing our pleas to fall before you because of our righteous acts, but because of your great compassion.

verses.rationale: Retains the urgent threefold Lord and successive imperatives.
verses.before: O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.”
verses.after: Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, because your city and your people bear your name.”
verses.tsw_comparator: O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, pay attention and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, because your city and your people are called by your name.”

verses.rationale: Preserves personal and communal confession and the repeated divine reference.
verses.before: While I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and causing my plea to fall before the LORD my God concerning the holy mountain of my God—
verses.after: I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my plea before the LORD my God concerning my God’s holy mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: While I was still speaking and praying and confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel and causing my plea to fall before the LORD my God concerning the holy mountain of my God—

verses.rationale: Keeps the man designation and offering time; the difficult flight expression receives a note.
verses.before: while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at first, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening offering.
verses.after: While I was still speaking in prayer, Gabriel, the man I had seen in the earlier vision, came to me in swift flight at about the time of the evening offering.
verses.tsw_comparator: while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at first, came to me in swift flight about the time of the evening offering.

verses.rationale: Preserves the double cognitive purpose of Gabriel’s arrival.
verses.before: He made me understand and spoke with me and said, “Daniel, now I have come out to give you insight and understanding.
verses.after: He instructed me and said, “Daniel, I have now come to give you insight and understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made me understand and spoke with me and said, “Daniel, now I have come out to give you insight and understanding.

verses.rationale: Keeps the timing, affectionate designation, and paired commands.
verses.before: At the beginning of your pleas a word went out, and I have come to declare it, for you are greatly beloved. So consider the word and understand the vision.
verses.after: A word went out when you began your pleas, and I have come to tell you, because you are greatly treasured. So consider the word and understand the vision.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the beginning of your pleas a word went out, and I have come to declare it, for you are greatly beloved. So consider the word and understand the vision.

verses.rationale: Preserves six purposes and the reading-note end-sin sense, with sevens and holy referent explained in notes.
verses.before: “Seventy sevens are decreed for your people and your holy city, to finish transgression, to seal up sin, to make atonement for guilt, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal vision and prophet, and to anoint a Most Holy thing.
verses.after: “Seventy sevens have been decreed for your people and your holy city: to restrain rebellion, bring sin to an end, make atonement for wrongdoing, bring everlasting righteousness, seal vision and prophet, and anoint a most holy place.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Seventy sevens are decreed for your people and your holy city, to finish transgression, to seal up sin, to make atonement for guilt, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal vision and prophet, and to anoint a Most Holy thing.

verses.rationale: Follows the major Hebrew pause after seven, keeping the two periods distinct and the ruler unnamed.
verses.before: Know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a ruler, there will be seven sevens; and for sixty-two sevens it will be rebuilt, with square and moat, but in troubled times.
verses.after: Know and understand: from the issuing of a word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed ruler comes, there will be seven sevens. For sixty-two sevens it will be rebuilt, with square and trench, but in troubled times.
verses.tsw_comparator: Know and understand: from the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a ruler, there will be seven sevens; and for sixty-two sevens it will be rebuilt, with square and moat, but in troubled times.

verses.rationale: Retains the indefinite anointed one, deprivation, flood, and ambiguous final referents.
verses.before: After the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off and have nothing. The people of a ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come with a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.
verses.after: After the sixty-two sevens, an anointed one will be cut off and have nothing. The people of a ruler who is to come will destroy the city and sanctuary. Its end will come with a flood; war will continue to the end. Desolations have been decreed.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the sixty-two sevens an anointed one will be cut off and have nothing. The people of a ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come with a flood, and until the end there will be war; desolations are decreed.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed he, literal wing image, and decreed judgment without adding an end-times scheme.
verses.before: He will make a strong covenant with many for one seven, and for half of the seven he will cause sacrifice and offering to cease. And upon the wing of detestable things will come one who makes desolate, until the decreed end is poured out upon the desolator.”
verses.after: He will make a covenant strong for the many for one seven. Halfway through the seven he will stop sacrifice and offering. On a wing of abominations will be one who devastates, until the decreed end is poured out upon the devastator.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He will make a strong covenant with many for one seven, and for half of the seven he will cause sacrifice and offering to cease. And upon the wing of detestable things will come one who makes desolate, until the decreed end is poured out upon the desolator.”

verses.rationale: Retains both names and the difficult conflict expression without turning it into a date calculation.
verses.before: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The word was true and concerned a great conflict. He understood the word and had understanding of the vision.
verses.after: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a message was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The message was true and concerned a great conflict. He understood the message and gained understanding of the vision.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, whose name was called Belteshazzar. The word was true and concerned a great conflict. He understood the word and had understanding of the vision.

verses.rationale: Keeps first-person transition and complete weeks of mourning.
verses.before: In those days I, Daniel, had been mourning for three full weeks.
verses.after: At that time I, Daniel, had been mourning for three full weeks.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those days I, Daniel, had been mourning for three full weeks.

verses.rationale: Preserves all abstentions without implying a total fast.
verses.before: I ate no desirable food; meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all until three full weeks were completed.
verses.after: I ate no rich food, no meat or wine passed my lips, and I used no oil on my body until the three full weeks were over.
verses.tsw_comparator: I ate no desirable food; meat and wine did not enter my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all until three full weeks were completed.

verses.rationale: Retains the exact date and identifies the Hebrew river name conventionally.
verses.before: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while I was beside the bank of the great river—that is, the Tigris—
verses.after: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was beside the great river, the Tigris.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, while I was beside the bank of the great river—that is, the Tigris—

verses.rationale: Keeps linen, gold origin, and waist placement without emending the place name.
verses.before: I lifted my eyes and looked, and look, there was a man clothed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.
verses.after: I looked up and saw a man dressed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.
verses.tsw_comparator: I lifted my eyes and looked, and behold, there was a man clothed in linen, with a belt of gold from Uphaz around his waist.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sequence of visual and auditory comparisons.
verses.before: His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like torches of fire, his arms and feet like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
verses.after: His body was like beryl, his face like lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, and his arms and legs like polished bronze. The sound of his words was like the roar of a multitude.
verses.tsw_comparator: His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like torches of fire, his arms and feet like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes seeing from the fear experienced by companions.
verses.before: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.
verses.after: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men with me did not see it, but a great terror fell on them, and they fled to hide.
verses.tsw_comparator: I, Daniel, alone saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see the vision, but a great trembling fell upon them, and they fled to hide themselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps both statements of lost strength and the bodily alteration.
verses.before: So I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; my splendor was turned into ruin, and I retained no strength.
verses.after: I was left alone, looking at this great vision. All my strength drained away; my appearance changed for the worse, and I had no strength left.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I was left alone and saw this great vision. No strength remained in me; my splendor was turned into ruin, and I retained no strength.

verses.rationale: Retains hearing before the deep-sleep collapse.
verses.before: Then I heard the sound of his words, and when I heard the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face to the ground.
verses.after: I heard the sound of his words. As I listened, I fell into a deep sleep, facedown on the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I heard the sound of his words, and when I heard the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face to the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves the partial rising before the later command to stand.
verses.before: And look, a hand touched me and made me tremble on my hands and knees.
verses.after: Then a hand touched me and set me trembling on my hands and knees.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, a hand touched me and made me tremble on my hands and knees.

verses.rationale: Keeps cherished address, sent status, and trembling obedience.
verses.before: He said to me, “Daniel, greatly beloved man, understand the words that I speak to you and stand upright, for now I have been sent to you.” When he spoke this word to me, I stood trembling.
verses.after: He said, “Daniel, greatly treasured man, understand the words I am speaking to you and stand upright, for I have now been sent to you.” As he said this, I stood trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, “Daniel, greatly beloved man, understand the words that I speak to you and stand upright, for now I have been sent to you.” When he spoke this word to me, I stood trembling.

verses.rationale: Preserves the immediate hearing despite delayed arrival.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.
verses.after: He said, “Do not be afraid, Daniel. From the first day you set your heart on understanding and humbled yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come because of your words.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Do not fear, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard, and I have come because of your words.

verses.rationale: Keeps the pinned first-person remained and plural kings rather than silently substituting left-him language.
verses.before: “But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me twenty-one days. Then look, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there with the kings of Persia.
verses.after: But the prince of the kingdom of Persia opposed me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I remained there beside the kings of Persia.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But the prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me twenty-one days. Then behold, Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there with the kings of Persia.

verses.rationale: Retains the people-centered purpose and open future timing.
verses.before: I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns days still to come.”
verses.after: I have come to help you understand what will happen to your people in the days to come, for the vision concerns days still ahead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the latter days, for the vision concerns days still to come.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed bodily reaction and inability to speak.
verses.before: When he had spoken these words with me, I set my face toward the ground and became mute.
verses.after: As he spoke these words to me, I lowered my face to the ground and was speechless.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he had spoken these words with me, I set my face toward the ground and became mute.

verses.rationale: Preserves the human likeness and touch enabling speech without naming an additional figure.
verses.before: And look, one in the likeness of the children of humanity touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth and spoke and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision pains have come upon me, and I retain no strength.
verses.after: Then someone with a human likeness touched my lips. I opened my mouth and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, the vision has overwhelmed me with anguish, and I have no strength left.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, one in the likeness of the children of humanity touched my lips. Then I opened my mouth and spoke and said to the one standing before me, “My lord, because of the vision pains have come upon me, and I retain no strength.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deferential doubled designation and bodily distress.
verses.before: How can this servant of my lord speak with this lord of mine? For as for me, no strength remains in me now, and no breath remains in me.”
verses.after: How can this servant of my lord speak with someone like my lord? My strength is gone, and no breath remains in me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: How can this servant of my lord speak with this lord of mine? For as for me, no strength remains in me now, and no breath remains in me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves another touch and its effect.
verses.before: Then again one having the appearance of a human being touched me and strengthened me.
verses.after: Again the one with a human appearance touched me and strengthened me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then again one having the appearance of a human being touched me and strengthened me.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated encouragement and response rather than reducing it to reassurance.
verses.before: He said, “Do not fear, greatly beloved man. Peace to you. Be strong, yes, be strong!” When he spoke with me, I was strengthened and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”
verses.after: “Do not be afraid, greatly treasured man,” he said. “Peace to you. Be strong! Be strong!” As he spoke, I gained strength and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Do not fear, greatly beloved man. Peace to you. Be strong, yes, be strong!” When he spoke with me, I was strengthened and said, “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the question and sequence of unnamed celestial conflict.
verses.before: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, look, the prince of Greece will come.
verses.after: He said, “Do you know why I have come to you? Soon I must return to fight the prince of Persia. When I go out, the prince of Greece will come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Do you know why I have come to you? And now I will return to fight with the prince of Persia. When I go out, behold, the prince of Greece will come.

verses.rationale: Keeps the written record and Michael’s relation to Daniel’s people.
verses.before: Yet I will tell you what is inscribed in the book of truth. There is no one who strengthens himself with me against these except Michael, your prince.”
verses.after: But I will tell you what is recorded in the writing of truth. No one stands with me against these except Michael, your prince.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will tell you what is inscribed in the book of truth. There is no one who strengthens himself with me against these except Michael, your prince.”

verses.rationale: Continues the heavenly speaker; leaves the pronoun’s antecedent unresolved.
verses.before: “And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood to strengthen and protect him.
verses.after: “In the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood to strengthen and protect him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood to strengthen and protect him.

verses.rationale: Preserves three plus fourth and wealth-driven mobilization.
verses.before: And now I will tell you the truth. Look, three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will become far richer than all of them. When he becomes strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
verses.after: “Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and a fourth will become far richer than all the others. When his wealth has made him powerful, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now I will tell you the truth. Behold, three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will become far richer than all of them. When he becomes strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unnamed ruler and unrestricted power.
verses.before: Then a mighty king will arise. He will rule with great dominion and do according to his will.
verses.after: Then a mighty king will arise. He will rule a vast realm and do as he pleases.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then a mighty king will arise. He will rule with great dominion and do according to his will.

verses.rationale: Preserves fragmentation, excluded descendants, and uprooting.
verses.before: But when he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of the heavens, but not to his descendants and not according to the dominion with which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these.
verses.after: But as he rises, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven. It will not pass to his descendants or retain the power with which he ruled. His kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides them.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of the heavens, but not to his descendants and not according to the dominion with which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the commander’s rise without supplying historical names.
verses.before: “The king of the south will become strong, but one of his officials will become stronger than he and rule. His dominion will be a great dominion.
verses.after: “The king of the south will grow strong, but one of his commanders will become stronger than he is and rule an even greater realm.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The king of the south will become strong, but one of his officials will become stronger than he and rule. His dominion will be a great dominion.

verses.rationale: Retains the woman’s fate and difficult family/support clauses with notes.
verses.before: At the end of years they will join themselves together. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain the strength of her arm, and he and his arm will not stand. She will be given up, along with people who brought her, the one who fathered her, and the one who supported her in those times.
verses.after: After some years they will form an alliance. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement. But she will not retain her strength, nor will he and his strength endure. She will be handed over, along with those who brought her, her father, and the one who supported her in those times.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of years they will join themselves together. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not retain the strength of her arm, and he and his arm will not stand. She will be given up, along with those who brought her, the one who fathered her, and the one who supported her in those times.

verses.rationale: Preserves the family-tree image and military success.
verses.before: “But a branch from her roots will arise in his place. He will come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north. He will act against them and prevail.
verses.after: A shoot from her roots will rise in his place. He will advance against the army, enter the northern king’s fortress, and deal with them successfully.
verses.tsw_comparator: “But a branch from her roots will arise in his place. He will come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north. He will act against them and prevail.

verses.rationale: Keeps Egypt explicit and the pause after seizure of sacred objects.
verses.before: Even their gods, with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold, he will carry captive to Egypt. For some years he will stand away from the king of the north.
verses.after: He will even carry their gods, cast images, and precious silver and gold vessels into captivity in Egypt. For some years he will leave the king of the north alone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even their gods, with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold, he will carry captive to Egypt. For some years he will stand away from the king of the north.

verses.rationale: Makes the inferred northern subject clear for the movement south and back.
verses.before: Then the king of the north will come into the kingdom of the king of the south but will return to his own land.
verses.after: Then the king of the north will enter the southern king’s realm but return to his own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of the north will come into the kingdom of the king of the south but will return to his own land.

verses.rationale: Follows the plural sons reading and subsequent singular advance.
verses.before: “His sons will stir themselves up and gather a multitude of great forces. One will surely come and overflow and pass through, and again he will carry the war as far as his fortress.
verses.after: His sons will prepare for war and gather a vast army. One will advance, flooding through, then renew the fighting as far as the fortress.
verses.tsw_comparator: “His sons will stir themselves up and gather a multitude of great forces. One will surely come and overflow and pass through, and again he will carry the war as far as his fortress.

verses.rationale: Clarifies alternating kings while preserving the army’s defeat.
verses.before: Then the king of the south will become enraged and go out and fight with him, with the king of the north. He will raise a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.
verses.after: The king of the south will rage and go out to fight the king of the north. The northern king will raise a great army, but it will be handed over to his opponent.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of the south will become enraged and go out and fight with him, with the king of the north. He will raise a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps pride, great casualties, and impermanent victory.
verses.before: When the multitude is carried away, his heart will be lifted up. He will cause tens of thousands to fall, but he will not prevail.
verses.after: When the army is carried off, the southern king’s heart will grow proud. He will bring down tens of thousands, but his strength will not endure.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the multitude is carried away, his heart will be lifted up. He will cause tens of thousands to fall, but he will not prevail.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed larger force and elapsed years.
verses.before: “For the king of the north will again raise a multitude greater than the first, and after some years he will surely come with a great army and abundant supplies.
