verses.after: The king of the north will return with an army larger than before. After some years, he will advance with a great army and abundant supplies.
verses.tsw_comparator: “For the king of the north will again raise a multitude greater than the first, and after some years he will surely come with a great army and abundant supplies.

verses.rationale: Keeps Daniel’s people involved without endorsing the violent faction.
verses.before: In those times many will rise against the king of the south. Violent men from your people will lift themselves up to establish the vision, but they will stumble.
verses.after: “In those times many will rise against the king of the south. Violent men among your own people will also rise to fulfill a vision, but they will stumble.
verses.tsw_comparator: In those times many will rise against the king of the south. Violent men from your people will lift themselves up to establish the vision, but they will stumble.

verses.rationale: Preserves siege method and failure of elite defenders.
verses.before: Then the king of the north will come, build up a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the south will not stand, even his chosen people will have no strength to stand.
verses.after: The king of the north will come, build a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The southern forces will not stand; even their picked troops will lack the strength to resist.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king of the north will come, build up a siege ramp, and capture a fortified city. The forces of the south will not stand, even his chosen people will have no strength to stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the land’s epithet and destructive agency.
verses.before: The one who comes against him will do according to his will, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.
verses.after: The invader will do as he pleases, and no one will withstand him. He will stand in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one who comes against him will do according to his will, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the Beautiful Land, with destruction in his hand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the political use of the woman and failure without inventing motives for her.
verses.before: “He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and an agreement will be with him. He will act and give him the daughter of women to destroy it, but she will not stand with him or be for him.
verses.after: He will resolve to come with the strength of his entire kingdom and make an agreement. He will give a daughter to the other king to bring ruin, but she will not stand with him or serve his purpose.
verses.tsw_comparator: “He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and an agreement will be with him. He will act and give him the daughter of women to destroy it, but she will not stand with him or be for him.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated reproach and reversal; difficult syntax is noted.
verses.before: Then he will turn his face toward the coastlands and capture many, but a commander will make his reproach cease; indeed, he will turn his reproach back upon him.
verses.after: Then he will turn toward the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to his insolence and turn that insolence back upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he will turn his face toward the coastlands and capture many, but a commander will make his reproach cease; indeed, he will turn his reproach back upon him.

verses.rationale: Preserves the threefold final collapse.
verses.before: Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and not be found.
verses.after: He will turn back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be found no more.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he will turn his face toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and not be found.

verses.rationale: Keeps the obscure royal-splendor expression and unusual death description.
verses.before: “Then one will arise in his place who sends an exactor through the glory of the kingdom, but within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.
verses.after: “In his place will arise one who sends an exactor through the splendor of the kingdom. Within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then one will arise in his place who sends an exactor through the glory of the kingdom, but within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves lack of legitimate honor and deceptive accession.
verses.before: In his place a despised one will arise, to whom they did not give the majesty of kingship. He will come in a time of ease and seize the kingdom through intrigue.
verses.after: In his place a despised person will arise, one who has not been given royal honor. He will come in while all is quiet and seize the kingdom through intrigue.
verses.tsw_comparator: In his place a despised one will arise, to whom they did not give the majesty of kingship. He will come in a time of ease and seize the kingdom through intrigue.

verses.rationale: Retains the flood wordplay and unnamed covenant prince.
verses.before: Forces like a flood will be swept away from before him and broken, and also a prince of the covenant.
verses.after: Flooding forces will be swept away before him and broken, along with a prince of the covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Forces like a flood will be swept away from before him and broken, and also a prince of the covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps deceit after agreement and the small supporting people.
verses.before: From the time an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will rise and become strong with a small people.
verses.after: After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will rise to power with only a small following.
verses.tsw_comparator: From the time an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will rise and become strong with a small people.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancestral comparison, three kinds of wealth, and limited duration.
verses.before: In a time of ease he will enter the richest parts of the province and do what his fathers and his fathers’ fathers did not do. Plunder, spoil, and possessions he will scatter among them. Against fortresses he will devise his plans, but only for a time.
verses.after: While all is quiet, he will enter the richest parts of the province and do what neither his fathers nor his fathers’ fathers did. He will distribute plunder, spoil, and wealth among them and devise plans against fortresses—but only for a time.
verses.tsw_comparator: In a time of ease he will enter the richest parts of the province and do what his fathers and his fathers’ fathers did not do. Plunder, spoil, and possessions he will scatter among them. Against fortresses he will devise his plans, but only for a time.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the two large forces and the role of conspiracy.
verses.before: “He will stir up his power and his heart against the king of the south with a great army. The king of the south will stir himself to battle with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he will not stand, for plans will be devised against him.
verses.after: He will rouse his strength and courage against the king of the south with a great army. The southern king will wage war with an exceedingly large and powerful army, but he will not stand, because schemes will be devised against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: “He will stir up his power and his heart against the king of the south with a great army. The king of the south will stir himself to battle with an exceedingly great and mighty army, but he will not stand, for plans will be devised against him.

verses.rationale: Preserves betrayal by table companions and military losses.
verses.before: People who eat his delicacies will break him, and his army will overflow, and many will fall slain.
verses.after: Those who eat his rich food will break him. His army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who eat his delicacies will break him, and his army will overflow, and many will fall slain.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared deceit, shared table, and the limit upon their plans.
verses.before: As for the two kings, their hearts will be toward evil. At one table they will speak lies, but it will not prosper, for the end is still for the appointed time.
verses.after: Both kings will have evil in their hearts. They will sit at one table and speak lies, but it will accomplish nothing, for the end still awaits its appointed time.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the two kings, their hearts will be toward evil. At one table they will speak lies, but it will not prosper, for the end is still for the appointed time.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the northern subject while retaining the repeated return.
verses.before: “Then he will return to his land with great possessions, but his heart will be against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his land.
verses.after: The northern king will return to his land with great wealth, his heart set against the holy covenant. He will take action and return to his own land.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Then he will return to his land with great possessions, but his heart will be against the holy covenant. He will act and return to his land.

verses.rationale: Keeps the temporal contrast without supplying battle names.
verses.before: At the appointed time he will return and come into the south, but this latter time will not be like the former.
verses.after: “At the appointed time he will invade the south again, but this later campaign will not be like the first.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the appointed time he will return and come into the south, but this latter time will not be like the former.

verses.rationale: Retains Kittim and both covenant references without replacing them with historical identifications.
verses.before: For ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart and turn back. He will become furious against the holy covenant and act. He will return and give attention to people who abandon the holy covenant.
verses.after: Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart. He will turn back and vent his fury on the holy covenant, taking action. On his return he will pay attention to those who abandon the holy covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart and turn back. He will become furious against the holy covenant and act. He will return and give attention to those who abandon the holy covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps the four hostile actions and recurring abomination designation.
verses.before: “Forces from him will arise and profane the sanctuary fortress. They will remove the continual offering and set up the detestable thing that makes desolate.
verses.after: Forces sent by him will arise, profane the sanctuary-fortress, remove the regular offering, and set up the abomination that devastates.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Forces from him will arise and profane the sanctuary fortress. They will remove the continual offering and set up the detestable thing that makes desolate.

verses.rationale: Preserves contrast between seduction and active steadfastness.
verses.before: People who act wickedly against the covenant he will make profane by smooth words, but the people who know their God will stand firm and act.
verses.after: With smooth words he will corrupt those who violate the covenant. But the people who know their God will stand firm and act.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will make profane by smooth words, but the people who know their God will stand firm and act.

verses.rationale: Keeps instruction and suffering together, including all four forms of harm.
verses.before: Those among the people who have insight will make many understand, though they will stumble by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder, for days.
verses.after: The discerning among the people will give understanding to many. Yet for a time they will fall by sword and flame, captivity and plunder.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those among the people who have insight will make many understand, though they will stumble by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder, for days.

verses.rationale: Preserves limited help and deceptive association.
verses.before: When they stumble, they will be helped with a little help, and many will join themselves to them with smooth words.
verses.after: When they fall, they will receive a little help, but many will join them insincerely.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they stumble, they will be helped with a little help, and many will join themselves to them with smooth words.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult refining purpose and its three verbs.
verses.before: Some of those with insight will stumble, to refine them, purify them, and make them white until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.
verses.after: Some of the discerning will fall, to refine, purify, and cleanse them until the time of the end, for it still awaits the appointed time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Some of those with insight will stumble, to refine them, purify them, and make them white until the time of the end, for it is still for the appointed time.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-exaltation and the boundary placed on success.
verses.before: “The king will do according to his will. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god and speak extraordinary things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the indignation is completed, for what is decreed will be done.
verses.after: “The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt and magnify himself above every god, speak astonishing things against the God of gods, and prosper until the wrath is finished. What has been decreed will be done.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The king will do according to his will. He will exalt himself and magnify himself above every god and speak extraordinary things against the God of gods. He will prosper until the indignation is completed, for what is decreed will be done.

verses.rationale: Leaves desire of women open rather than identifying a deity or sexual preference.
verses.before: He will give no attention to the gods of his fathers or to the desire of women or to any god, for he will magnify himself above all.
verses.after: He will pay no attention to the gods of his ancestors, to the desire of women, or to any god, because he will magnify himself above them all.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will give no attention to the gods of his fathers or to the desire of women or to any god, for he will magnify himself above all.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unfamiliar deity and four offerings.
verses.before: Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses in its place, a god whom his fathers did not know. He will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and desirable things.
verses.after: Instead he will honor a god of fortresses. He will honor a god his ancestors did not know with gold, silver, precious stones, and costly gifts.
verses.tsw_comparator: Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses in its place, a god whom his fathers did not know. He will honor it with gold, silver, precious stones, and desirable things.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult recognition and payment clauses with their uncertainty noted.
verses.before: He will act against the strongest fortresses with a foreign god. Whoever acknowledges him he will multiply with honor, and he will cause them to rule over many and divide land for a price.
verses.after: He will act against strong fortresses with a foreign god. Those he acknowledges he will greatly honor, giving them authority over many and dividing land for a price.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will act against the strongest fortresses with a foreign god. Whoever acknowledges him he will multiply with honor, and he will cause them to rule over many and divide land for a price.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named opponents and unspecified pronouns without forcing all identities.
verses.before: “At the time of the end, the king of the south will push against him, and the king of the north will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will enter lands, overflow, and pass through.
verses.after: “At the time of the end, the king of the south will clash with him. The king of the north will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will invade lands, flooding through them.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At the time of the end, the king of the south will push against him, and the king of the north will storm against him with chariots, horsemen, and many ships. He will enter lands, overflow, and pass through.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three exceptions and land epithet.
verses.before: He will enter the Beautiful Land, and many will stumble. But these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.
verses.after: He will enter the Beautiful Land, and many will fall. But Edom, Moab, and the foremost of the Ammonites will escape his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will enter the Beautiful Land, and many will stumble. But these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the hand image and Egypt’s explicit exclusion from escape.
verses.before: He will stretch out his hand against lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
verses.after: He will stretch out his hand against the lands, and Egypt will not escape.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will stretch out his hand against lands, and the land of Egypt will not escape.

verses.rationale: Preserves treasures and the named accompanying peoples.
verses.before: He will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and over all the desirable things of Egypt, and the Libyans and Cushites will follow in his steps.
verses.after: He will control Egypt’s hidden stores of gold and silver and all its treasures. Libyans and Cushites will follow in his steps.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will rule over the hidden treasures of gold and silver and over all the desirable things of Egypt, and the Libyans and Cushites will follow in his steps.

verses.rationale: Keeps both directions and the intensified destruction language.
verses.before: But reports from the east and from the north will terrify him, and he will go out in great fury to destroy and devote many to destruction.
verses.after: But reports from the east and north will alarm him. He will go out in great fury to destroy and devote many to destruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: But reports from the east and from the north will terrify him, and he will go out in great fury to destroy and devote many to destruction.

verses.rationale: Preserves plural seas, the mountain, and unassisted ending.
verses.before: He will plant the tents of his royal pavilion between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and there will be no one to help him.
verses.after: He will pitch his royal tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, with no one to help him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will plant the tents of his royal pavilion between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and there will be no one to help him.

verses.rationale: Keeps Michael’s protective relation and the written-book qualification.
verses.before: “At that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over the children of your people. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will escape, everyone who is found written in the book.
verses.after: “At that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over your people. There will be a time of distress unlike any since a nation first existed. But at that time your people will escape—everyone found written in the book.
verses.tsw_comparator: “At that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over the children of your people. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will escape, everyone who is found written in the book.

verses.rationale: Preserves many, the bodily waking image, and both lasting outcomes.
verses.before: “Many of people who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, these to everlasting life and these to reproach and everlasting contempt.
verses.after: Many who sleep in the dusty ground will wake, some to everlasting life and others to shame and everlasting contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, these to everlasting life and these to reproach and everlasting contempt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two groups and celestial comparisons.
verses.before: People who have insight will shine like the brightness of the expanse, and people who make the many righteous like the stars forever and ever.
verses.after: The discerning will shine like the brightness of the expanse, and those who lead many to righteousness like the stars forever and ever.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who have insight will shine like the brightness of the expanse, and those who make the many righteous like the stars forever and ever.

verses.rationale: Retains movement and increasing knowledge without adding a modern technological reference.
verses.before: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will go back and forth, and knowledge will increase.”
verses.after: But you, Daniel, close up the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will go to and fro, and knowledge will increase.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will go back and forth, and knowledge will increase.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the two figures and opposing banks.
verses.before: Then I, Daniel, looked, and look, two others were standing, one on this bank of the river and one on the other bank of the river.
verses.after: Then I, Daniel, looked and saw two others standing, one on each bank of the river.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others were standing, one on this bank of the river and one on the other bank of the river.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the asking figure without naming him and preserves the question’s scope.
verses.before: One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long until the end of these wonders?”
verses.after: One asked the man dressed in linen, who was above the river’s waters, “How long until these astonishing things come to an end?”
verses.tsw_comparator: One said to the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, “How long until the end of these wonders?”

verses.rationale: Retains both raised hands, oath, symbolic duration, and broken communal power.
verses.before: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, and he raised his right hand and his left hand toward the heavens and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time. And when the shattering of the power of the holy people is completed, all these things will be completed.
verses.after: I heard the man dressed in linen, above the river’s waters. He raised his right and left hands to heaven and swore by the one who lives forever: “For a time, times, and half a time. When the shattering of the holy people’s power is finished, all these things will be completed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I heard the man clothed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, and he raised his right hand and his left hand toward the heavens and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times, and half a time. And when the shattering of the power of the holy people is completed, all these things will be completed.

verses.rationale: Keeps Daniel’s lack of understanding after hearing the explanation.
verses.before: I heard, but I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”
verses.after: I heard but did not understand. So I asked, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”
verses.tsw_comparator: I heard, but I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the refusal of further disclosure and repeated sealing.
verses.before: He said, “Go, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
verses.after: He said, “Go your way, Daniel, for the words are closed up and sealed until the time of the end.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said, “Go, Daniel, for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three refining terms and contrasting comprehension.
verses.before: Many will purify themselves, make themselves white, and be refined, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but those with insight will understand.
verses.after: Many will be purified, cleansed, and refined, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand; the discerning will understand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many will purify themselves, make themselves white, and be refined, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but those with insight will understand.

verses.rationale: Preserves the exact count without reconciling it to another period.
verses.before: “From the time the continual offering is removed and the detestable thing that makes desolate is set up, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.
verses.after: From the time the regular offering is removed and the abomination that devastates is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
verses.tsw_comparator: “From the time the continual offering is removed and the detestable thing that makes desolate is set up, there will be one thousand two hundred ninety days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct second count and endurance blessing.
verses.before: Happy is the one who waits and reaches one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.
verses.after: Happy is the one who waits and reaches the 1,335 days.
verses.tsw_comparator: Happy is the one who waits and reaches one thousand three hundred thirty-five days.

verses.rationale: Preserves rest, standing, and allotted portion without flattening the final hope.
verses.before: “But you, go your way until the end. You will rest, and you will stand for your lot at the end of the days.”
verses.after: But you, go on to the end. You will rest, then stand in your allotted place at the end of the days.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “But you, go your way until the end. You will rest, and you will stand for your lot at the end of the days.”

comparative_references.scope: All 287 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
